note_sections.t: Re-evaluation of prostate cancer diagnosis to discuss management options following recent PSA rise and prior biopsy results.

Recently retired civil engineer with a history of prostate cancer diagnosed on biopsy. PSA has steadily increased from 3.3 ng/mL in Nov 2022 to 7.5 ng/mL in Feb 2025. Patient reports severe lower urinary tract symptoms, IPSS score 30/35. He is married, lives with his partner, and cycles five times a week for commuting. He is an ex-smoker, quit in 2015. Recent appointments include memory clinic baseline screening and dermatology for actinic keratosis check. He prefers morning appointments due to public transport reliance.
On DRE, the prostate is non-palpable, consistent with cT1c. General examination is unremarkable, with stable vitals and no acute distress.
